prompt:
One shot sheet for an animated film: the one person in the reference images drawn 3 times in one row, left to right, in exactly this order:
1. seated on the low stool facing the viewer, the baby in her left arm, her right hand in its sleeve holding a small plain clay cup painted exactly #c9877e, milk #eadcc2 showing at its rim to the baby's lips, her head tilted toward the baby, a tender smile; her brown hair under the veil and her sandals painted exactly #c9877e.
2. seated exactly as in the first figure, the cup held the same at the baby's lips, the baby drinking with its eyes shut as two glad upward-curved ink lines and its cheeks lifted, the mother smiling.
3. seated exactly as the first figure, every line the same, the eyes closed in a blink: each eye a short downward-curved ink line, the mother's eyes closed and the baby's open.
The person, as described: The people are the young mother at the wedding feast and the baby she holds, never named. She is a young woman of slender build, about three and a third heads tall and nine tenths of a man's height, dressed in the Bible's own time: a long dusty-blue dress (#5f7fa8, its far side turned toward a deeper blue-violet #4c5687) to her ankles with long sleeves to the wrist, the same blue from each shoulder to each round warm-peach hand, never a cream or white sleeve; a cream veil (#eadcc2, its shade turned toward lavender #c8bdd6) over her brown hair, falling to her shoulders; brown sandals. Her skin warm peach (#f2b27c, its shade a rosy violet #c9877e); a face of three marks: two short brows, two small dark oval eyes and a one-line mouth. The baby is about two heads tall, wrapped in a cream wrap (#eadcc2) to its feet, a round warm-peach face with the same three marks and a small tuft of brown hair; its round hands at the ends of the wrap's folds. Standing alone on a turnaround, she stands at rest with both arms hanging in their sleeves; with the baby, she holds it on her hip with exactly two hands, both on the baby: one under it, one at its back, unless a pose gives one hand a cup. Each hand at the end of its sleeve, no thumbs, no fingers. No pattern, trim or embroidery. What they hold, and only where a pose names it: a small plain clay cup. Where the description names an order of figures, the order above holds.
Continuity: this is one person drawn 3 times in one pass, so every figure has the same face, the same head size, the same body proportions, the same colours, the same line weight and the same shading; only the turn and the pose change. All figures stand on one baseline at one size, the soles of every figure on the same line.
House rules: each hand is a plain round circle of skin at the end of its sleeve, no thumb and no fingers. Sleeves run to the wrist in every figure, the raised arm too: no bare arm or forearm ever shows. One bold warm-dark outline of even weight round each figure. One flat shade per colour: no gradient, no texture, no airbrush, no highlight.
Clothes: every part of the clothes is outlined in the same ink #1b0b03 as the figure; a fold on cloth is a line in that cloth's own shade; no rose, pink or skin colour anywhere on the clothes, skin colour only on the face, neck, hands and feet.
Paint with exactly these colours: the outline ink #1b0b03; skin #f2b27c with its shaded side #c9877e; dress #5f7fa8 with its shaded side #4c5687; veil #eadcc2 with its shaded side #c8bdd6.
The ground: one flat colour, #a6dcae, everywhere behind and between the figures, with wide clear ground between each figure and the next (a reaching or raised hand too) so no figure touches or nears another; no glow, halo or soft light round any figure; no floor, no cast shadow, no text, no frame.
The narration's words appear only as full-screen cards: nothing in the picture carries lettering.
A held prop is named in the pose words and is the same prop, the same size and the same colours in every figure that holds it. No prop carries text, letters, numbers or marks.
Where a pose turns the head, it turns exactly as the pose words say, toward the viewer's left or right as written, whatever way the description or the reference images face.
The seat is one low plain wooden stool painted exactly #c9877e, flat, with no shade of its own.
Each seated figure is drawn whole, from the top of the head to the soles of both feet resting flat on the ground line: no table, bench or anything else in front of the figure hides any part of it.
